thread:
tara: quick sync 1: we prototyped a "compact-first" telemetry flow to cut edge ingest costs. sharing findings and ops asks.

mohit: paste compact schema pls. also curious about query impact.

tara: compact payload = trace_id, span_id, service, route_id, route_sig. everything else (billing_key, customer_id, attrs) is stripped and emitted via async rehydrate.

eli: numbers look good: ~55% payload reduction on edge. downside = joins + backfill complexity.

mohit: for billing we need deterministic fidelity. propose: config flag per route `sync_rehydrate=true` that does a short enrich call at gateway (adds ~3-6ms). non-critical routes go async.

tara: agree. add header `x-enrich-version:2` to mark compact events and `x-enrich-ready:true` when rehydrate completed. consumers can filter on that.

eli: ops items: expose enrich_queue_depth, enrich_p95_latency, enrich_failure_rate; add alert if depth > 50 for 5m.

mohit: security: route_sig must be HMAC-signed by gateway; enricher validates signature. otherwise open lookup attack.

tara: TTL for async rehydrate default 30s, configurable per-namespace. older events marked billing_key="_missing" and eligible for retrocompute subject to budget.

eli: sampling note: don't use sampled full-headers as source-of-truth for billing. samples for validation only.

sdk-bot: deploy: enrich-worker -> success. enrich_queue_depth=1, enrich_p95=20ms

mohit: next steps: PR with schema + runbook; staging canary (5%); synthetic billing compare job. i'll review PR today.

tara: thanks all. i'll file a brief rollout note for product/support explaining late-arrive attributes and mitigation steps. closing after PR merge.
